question.prompt:
In trapezoid \(ABCD,\) sides \(AB\) and \(CD\) are parallel, and diagonal \(BD\) and side \(AD\) have equal length. If \(\angle DCB=110^\circ\) and \(\angle CBD=30^\circ,\) then \(\angle ADB=\)

[Figure 1](figures/1981_AMC_12_Q05_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The equal lengths \(AD=BD\) make triangle \(ADB\) isosceles, so finding either base angle will determine the requested angle. First use the two known angles in triangle \(DCB\):
\[
\angle CDB=180^\circ-110^\circ-30^\circ=40^\circ.
\]
Because \(AB\parallel CD\), transversal \(BD\) gives equal alternate interior angles \(\angle ABD=\angle CDB=40^\circ\). In triangle \(ADB\), the equal sides \(AD\) and \(BD\) have opposite equal angles, so \(\angle DAB=\angle ABD=40^\circ\). Therefore
\[
\angle ADB=180^\circ-40^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{100^\circ},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Transfer an angle into the isosceles triangle
